Yet for your sake we face death all day long;
Awake, Lord! Why do you sleep?
Why do you hide your face
We are brought down to the dust;
Rise up and help us;
My heart is stirred by a noble theme
You are the most excellent of men
Gird your sword on your side, you mighty one;
In your majesty ride forth victoriously
Let your sharp arrows pierce the hearts of the king’s enemies;
Your throne, O God, will last for ever and ever;
You love righteousness and hate wickedness;
All your robes are fragrant with myrrh and aloes and cassia;
Daughters of kings are among your honoured women;
Listen, daughter, and pay careful attention:
Let the king be enthralled by your beauty;
The city of Tyre will come with a gift,
All glorious is the princess within her chamber;
In embroidered garments she is led to the king;
Led in with joy and gladness,
Your sons will take the place of your fathers;
I will perpetuate your memory through all generations;
God is our refuge and strength,
Therefore we will not fear, though the earth give way
though its waters roar and foam
There is a river whose streams make glad the city of God,
God is within her, she will not fall;
Nations are in uproar, kingdoms fall;
The Lord Almighty is with us;
Come and see what the Lord has done,
He makes wars cease
He says, ‘Be still, and know that I am God;
The Lord Almighty is with us;
Clap your hands, all you nations;
For the Lord Most High is awesome,
He subdued nations under us,
He chose our inheritance for us,
God has ascended amid shouts of joy,
Sing praises to God, sing praises;
For God is the King of all the earth;
God reigns over the nations;
The nobles of the nations assemble
Great is the Lord, and most worthy of praise,
Beautiful in its loftiness,
God is in her citadels;
When the kings joined forces,
they saw her and were astounded;
Trembling seized them there,
You destroyed them like ships of Tarshish
As we have heard,
Within your temple, O God,
Like your name, O God,
Mount Zion rejoices,
Walk about Zion, go round her,
consider well her ramparts,
For this God is our God for ever and ever;
Hear this, all you peoples;
both low and high,
My mouth will speak words of wisdom;
I will turn my ear to a proverb;
Why should I fear when evil days come,
those who trust in their wealth
No-one can redeem the life of another
the ransom for a life is costly,
so that they should live on for ever
For all can see that the wise die,
Their tombs will remain their houses for ever,
People, despite their wealth, do not endure;
This is the fate of those who trust in themselves,
They are like sheep and are destined to die;
But God will redeem me from the realm of the dead;
Do not be overawed when others grow rich,
for they will take nothing with them when they die,
Though while they live they count themselves blessed –
they will join those who have gone before them,
People who have wealth but lack understanding
The Mighty One, God, the Lord,
From Zion, perfect in beauty,
Our God comes
He summons the heavens above,
‘Gather to me this consecrated people,
And the heavens proclaim his righteousness,
‘Listen, my people, and I will speak;
I bring no charges against you concerning your sacrifices
I have no need of a bull from your stall
for every animal of the forest is mine,
I know every bird in the mountains,
If I were hungry I would not tell you,
Do I eat the flesh of bulls
‘Sacrifice thank-offerings to God,
and call on me in the day of trouble;
But to the wicked person, God says:
You hate my instruction
When you see a thief, you join with him;
You use your mouth for evil
You sit and testify against your brother
When you did these things and I kept silent,
‘Consider this, you who forget God,
those who sacrifice thank-offerings honour me,
Have mercy on me, O God,
Wash away all my iniquity
For I know my transgressions,
Against you, you only, have I sinned
Surely I was sinful at birth,
Yet you desired faithfulness even in the womb;
Cleanse me with hyssop, and I shall be clean;
Let me hear joy and gladness;
Hide your face from my sins
Create in me a pure heart, O God,
Do not cast me from your presence
Restore to me the joy of your salvation
Then I will teach transgressors your ways,
Deliver me from the guilt of bloodshed, O God,
Open my lips, Lord,
You do not delight in sacrifice, or I would bring it;
My sacrifice, O God, is a broken spirit;
May it please you to prosper Zion,
Then you will delight in the sacrifices of the righteous,
Why do you boast of evil, you mighty hero?
You who practise deceit,
You love evil rather than good,
You love every harmful word,
Surely God will bring you down to everlasting ruin:
The righteous will see and fear;
‘Here now is the man
But I am like an olive tree
For what you have done I will always praise you
The fool says in his heart,
God looks down from heaven
Everyone has turned away, all have become corrupt;
Do all these evildoers know nothing?
But there they are, overwhelmed with dread,
Oh, that salvation for Israel would come out of Zion!
Save me, O God, by your name;
Hear my prayer, O God;
Arrogant foes are attacking me;
Surely God is my help;
Let evil recoil on those who slander me;
I will sacrifice a freewill offering to you;
You have delivered me from all my troubles,
Listen to my prayer, O God,
hear me and answer me.
because of what my enemy is saying,
My heart is in anguish within me;
Fear and trembling have beset me;
I said, ‘Oh, that I had the wings of a dove!
I would flee far away
I would hurry to my place of shelter,
Lord, confuse the wicked, confound their words,
Day and night they prowl about on its walls;
Destructive forces are at work in the city;
If an enemy were insulting me,
But it is you, a man like myself,
with whom I once enjoyed sweet fellowship
Let death take my enemies by surprise;
As for me, I call to God,
Evening, morning and noon
He rescues me unharmed
God, who is enthroned from of old,
My companion attacks his friends;
His talk is smooth as butter,
Cast your cares on the Lord
But you, God, will bring down the wicked
Be merciful to me, my God,
My adversaries pursue me all day long;
When I am afraid, I put my trust in you.
In God, whose word I praise –
All day long they twist my words;
They conspire, they lurk,
Because of their wickedness do not let them escape;
Record my misery;
Then my enemies will turn back
In God, whose word I praise,
in God I trust and am not afraid.
I am under vows to you, my God;
For you have delivered me from death
Have mercy on me, my God, have mercy on me,
I cry out to God Most High,
He sends from heaven and saves me,
I am in the midst of lions;
Be exalted, O God, above the heavens;
They spread a net for my feet –
My heart, O God, is steadfast,
Awake, my soul!
I will praise you, Lord, among the nations;
For great is your love, reaching to the heavens;
Be exalted, O God, above the heavens;
Do you rulers indeed speak justly?
No, in your heart you devise injustice,
Even from birth the wicked go astray;
Their venom is like the venom of a snake,
that will not heed the tune of the charmer,
Break the teeth in their mouths, O God;
Let them vanish like water that flows away;
May they be like a slug that melts away as it moves along,
Before your pots can feel the heat of the thorns –
The righteous will be glad when they are avenged,
Then people will say,
Deliver me from my enemies, O God;
Deliver me from evildoers
See how they lie in wait for me!
I have done no wrong, yet they are ready to attack me.
You, Lord God Almighty,
They return at evening,
See what they spew from their mouths –
But you laugh at them, Lord;
You are my strength, I watch for you;
my God on whom I can rely.
But do not kill them, Lord our shield,
For the sins of their mouths,
consume them in your wrath,
They return at evening,
They wander about for food
But I will sing of your strength,
You are my strength, I sing praise to you;
You have rejected us, God, and burst upon us;
You have shaken the land and torn it open;
You have shown your people desperate times;
But for those who fear you, you have raised a banner
Save us and help us with your right hand,
God has spoken from his sanctuary:
Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine;
Moab is my washbasin,
Who will bring me to the fortified city?
Is it not you, God, you who have now rejected us
Give us aid against the enemy,
With God we shall gain the victory,
Hear my cry, O God;
From the ends of the earth I call to you,
For you have been my refuge,
I long to dwell in your tent for ever
For you, God, have heard my vows;
Increase the days of the king’s life,
May he be enthroned in God’s presence for ever;
Then I will ever sing in praise of your name
Truly my soul finds rest in God;
Truly he is my rock and my salvation;
How long will you assault me?
Surely they intend to topple me
Yes, my soul, find rest in God;
Truly he is my rock and my salvation;
My salvation and my honour depend on God;
Trust in him at all times, you people;
Surely the lowborn are but a breath,
Do not trust in extortion
One thing God has spoken,
and with you, Lord, is unfailing love’;
You, God, are my God,
I have seen you in the sanctuary
Because your love is better than life,
I will praise you as long as I live,
I will be satisfied as with the richest of foods;
On my bed I remember you;
Because you are my help,
I cling to you;
Those who want to kill me will be destroyed;
They will be given over to the sword
But the king will rejoice in God;
Hear me, my God, as I voice my complaint;
Hide me from the conspiracy of the wicked,
They sharpen their tongues like swords
They shoot from ambush at the innocent;
They encourage each other in evil plans,
They plot injustice and say,
But God will shoot them with his arrows;
He will turn their own tongues against them
All people will fear;
The righteous will rejoice in the Lord
Praise awaits you, our God, in Zion;
You who answer prayer,
When we were overwhelmed by sins,
Blessed are those you choose
You answer us with awesome and righteous deeds,
who formed the mountains by your power,
who stilled the roaring of the seas,
The whole earth is filled with awe at your wonders;
You care for the land and water it;
You drench its furrows and level its ridges;
You crown the year with your bounty,
The grasslands of the wilderness overflow;
The meadows are covered with flocks
Shout for joy to God, all the earth!
Sing the glory of his name;
Say to God, ‘How awesome are your deeds!
All the earth bows down to you;
Come and see what God has done,
He turned the sea into dry land,
He rules for ever by his power,
Praise our God, all peoples,
he has preserved our lives
For you, God, tested us;
You brought us into prison
You let people ride over our heads;
I will come to your temple with burnt offerings
vows my lips promised and my mouth spoke
I will sacrifice fat animals to you
Come and hear, all you who fear God;
I cried out to him with my mouth;
If I had cherished sin in my heart,
but God has surely listened
Praise be to God,
May God be gracious to us and bless us
so that your ways may be known on earth,
May the peoples praise you, God;
May the nations be glad and sing for joy,
May the peoples praise you, God;
The land yields its harvest;
May God bless us still,
May God arise, may his enemies be scattered;
May you blow them away like smoke –
But may the righteous be glad
Sing to God, sing in praise of his name,
A father to the fatherless, a defender of widows,
God sets the lonely in families,
When you, God, went out before your people,
the earth shook, the heavens poured down rain,
You gave abundant showers, O God;
Your people settled in it,
The Lord announces the word,
‘Kings and armies flee in haste;
Even while you sleep among the sheepfolds,
When the Almighty scattered the kings in the land,
Mount Bashan, majestic mountain,
why gaze in envy, you rugged mountain,
The chariots of God are tens of thousands
When you ascended on high,
Praise be to the Lord, to God our Saviour,
Our God is a God who saves;
Surely God will crush the heads of his enemies,
The Lord says, ‘I will bring them from Bashan;
that your feet may wade in the blood of your foes,
Your procession, God, has come into view,
In front are the singers, after them the musicians;
Praise God in the great congregation;
There is the little tribe of Benjamin, leading them,
Summon your power, God;
Because of your temple at Jerusalem
Rebuke the beast among the reeds,
Envoys will come from Egypt;
Sing to God, you kingdoms of the earth,
to him who rides across the highest heavens, the ancient heavens,
Proclaim the power of God,
You, God, are awesome in your sanctuary;
Save me, O God,
I sink in the miry depths,
I am worn out calling for help;
Those who hate me without reason
You, God, know my folly;
Lord, the Lord Almighty,
For I endure scorn for your sake,
I am a foreigner to my own family,
for zeal for your house consumes me,
When I weep and fast,
when I put on sackcloth,
Those who sit at the gate mock me,
But I pray to you, Lord,
Rescue me from the mire,
Do not let the floodwaters engulf me
Answer me, Lord, out of the goodness of your love;
Do not hide your face from your servant;
Come near and rescue me;
You know how I am scorned, disgraced and shamed;
Scorn has broken my heart
They put gall in my food
May the table set before them become a snare;
May their eyes be darkened so that they cannot see,
Pour out your wrath on them;
May their place be deserted;
For they persecute those you wound
Charge them with crime upon crime;
May they be blotted out of the book of life
But as for me, afflicted and in pain –
I will praise God’s name in song
This will please the Lord more than an ox,
The poor will see and be glad –
The Lord hears the needy
Let heaven and earth praise him,
for God will save Zion
the children of his servants will inherit it,
Hasten, O God, to save me;
May those who want to take my life
May those who say to me, ‘Aha! Aha!’
But may all who seek you
But as for me, I am poor and needy;
In you, Lord, I have taken refuge;
In your righteousness, rescue me and deliver me;
Be my rock of refuge,
Deliver me, my God, from the hand of the wicked,
For you have been my hope, Sovereign Lord,
From my birth I have relied on you;
I have become a sign to many;
My mouth is filled with your praise,
Do not cast me away when I am old;
For my enemies speak against me;
They say, ‘God has forsaken him;
Do not be far from me, my God;
May my accusers perish in shame;
As for me, I shall always have hope;
My mouth will tell of your righteous deeds,
I will come and proclaim your mighty acts, Sovereign Lord;
Since my youth, God, you have taught me,
Even when I am old and grey,
Your righteousness, God, reaches to the heavens,
Though you have made me see troubles,
You will increase my honour
I will praise you with the harp
My lips will shout for joy
My tongue will tell of your righteous acts
Endow the king with your justice, O God,
May he judge your people in righteousness,
May the mountains bring prosperity to the people,
May he defend the afflicted among the people
May he endure as long as the sun,
May he be like rain falling on a mown field,
In his days may the righteous flourish
May he rule from sea to sea
May the desert tribes bow before him
May the kings of Tarshish and of distant shores
May all kings bow down to him
For he will deliver the needy who cry out,
He will take pity on the weak and the needy
He will rescue them from oppression and violence,
Long may he live!
May corn abound throughout the land;
May his name endure for ever;
Praise be to the Lord God, the God of Israel,
Praise be to his glorious name for ever;
This concludes the prayers of David son of Jesse.
Surely God is good to Israel,
But as for me, my feet had almost slipped;
For I envied the arrogant
They have no struggles;
They are free from common human burdens;
Therefore pride is their necklace;
From their callous hearts comes iniquity;
They scoff, and speak with malice;
Their mouths lay claim to heaven,
Therefore their people turn to them
They say, ‘How would God know?
This is what the wicked are like –
Surely in vain I have kept my heart pure
All day long I have been afflicted,
If I had spoken out like that,
When I tried to understand all this,
till I entered the sanctuary of God;
Surely you place them on slippery ground;
How suddenly are they destroyed,
They are like a dream when one awakes;
When my heart was grieved
I was senseless and ignorant;
Yet I am always with you;
You guide me with your counsel,
Whom have I in heaven but you?
My flesh and my heart may fail,
Those who are far from you will perish;
But as for me, it is good to be near God.
O God, why have you rejected us for ever?
Remember the nation you purchased long ago,
Turn your steps towards these everlasting ruins,
Your foes roared in the place where you met with us;
They behaved like men wielding axes
They smashed all the carved panelling
They burned your sanctuary to the ground;
They said in their hearts, ‘We will crush them completely!’
We are given no signs from God;
How long will the enemy mock you, God?
Why do you hold back your hand, your right hand?
But God is my King from long ago;
It was you who split open the sea by your power;
It was you who crushed the heads of Leviathan
It was you who opened up springs and streams;
The day is yours, and yours also the night;
It was you who set all the boundaries of the earth;
Remember how the enemy has mocked you, Lord,
Do not hand over the life of your dove to wild beasts;
Have regard for your covenant,
Do not let the oppressed retreat in disgrace;
Rise up, O God, and defend your cause;
Do not ignore the clamour of your adversaries,
We praise you, God,
You say, ‘I choose the appointed time;
When the earth and all its people quake,
To the arrogant I say, “Boast no more,”
Do not lift your horns against heaven;
No-one from the east or the west
It is God who judges:
In the hand of the Lord is a cup
As for me, I will declare this for ever;
who says, ‘I will cut off the horns of all the wicked,
God is renowned in Judah;
His tent is in Salem,
There he broke the flashing arrows,
You are radiant with light,
The valiant lie plundered,
At your rebuke, God of Jacob,
It is you alone who are to be feared.
From heaven you pronounced judgment,
when you, God, rose up to judge,
Surely your wrath against mankind brings you praise,
Make vows to the Lord your God and fulfil them;
He breaks the spirit of rulers;
I cried out to God for help;
When I was in distress, I sought the Lord;
I remembered you, God, and I groaned;
You kept my eyes from closing;
I thought about the former days,
I remembered my songs in the night.
‘Will the Lord reject for ever?
Has his unfailing love vanished for ever?
Has God forgotten to be merciful?
Then I thought, ‘To this I will appeal:
I will remember the deeds of the Lord;
I will consider all your works
Your ways, God, are holy.
You are the God who performs miracles;
With your mighty arm you redeemed your people,
The waters saw you, God,
The clouds poured down water,
Your thunder was heard in the whirlwind,
Your path led through the sea,
You led your people like a flock
My people, hear my teaching;
I will open my mouth with a parable;
things we have heard and known,
We will not hide them from their descendants;
He decreed statutes for Jacob
so that the next generation would know them,
Then they would put their trust in God
They would not be like their ancestors –
The men of Ephraim, though armed with bows,
they did not keep God’s covenant
They forgot what he had done,
He did miracles in the sight of their ancestors
He divided the sea and led them through;
He guided them with the cloud by day
He split the rocks in the wilderness
he brought streams out of a rocky crag
But they continued to sin against him,
They wilfully put God to the test
They spoke against God;
True, he struck the rock,
When the Lord heard them, he was furious;
for they did not believe in God
Yet he gave a command to the skies above
he rained down manna for the people to eat,
Human beings ate the bread of angels;
He let loose the east wind from the heavens
He rained meat down on them like dust,
He made them come down inside their camp,
They ate till they were gorged –
But before they turned from what they craved,
God’s anger rose against them;
In spite of all this, they kept on sinning;
So he ended their days in futility
Whenever God slew them, they would seek him;
They remembered that God was their Rock,
But then they would flatter him with their mouths,
their hearts were not loyal to him,
Yet he was merciful;
He remembered that they were but flesh,
How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness
Again and again they put God to the test;
They did not remember his power –
the day he displayed his signs in Egypt,
He turned their river into blood;
He sent swarms of flies that devoured them,
He gave their crops to the grasshopper,
He destroyed their vines with hail
He gave over their cattle to the hail,
He unleashed against them his hot anger,
He prepared a path for his anger;
He struck down all the firstborn of Egypt,
But he brought his people out like a flock;
He guided them safely, so they were unafraid;
And so he brought them to the border of his holy land,
He drove out nations before them
But they put God to the test
Like their ancestors they were disloyal and faithless,
They angered him with their high places;
When God heard them, he was furious;
He abandoned the tabernacle of Shiloh,
He sent the ark of his might into captivity,
He gave his people over to the sword;
Fire consumed their young men,
their priests were put to the sword,
Then the Lord awoke as from sleep,
He beat back his enemies;
Then he rejected the tents of Joseph,
but he chose the tribe of Judah,
He built his sanctuary like the heights,
He chose David his servant
from tending the sheep he brought him
And David shepherded them with integrity of heart;
O God, the nations have invaded your inheritance;
They have left the dead bodies of your servants
They have poured out blood like water
We are objects of contempt to our neighbours,
How long, Lord? Will you be angry for ever?
Pour out your wrath on the nations
for they have devoured Jacob
Do not hold against us the sins of past generations;
Help us, God our Saviour,
Why should the nations say,
May the groans of the prisoners come before you;
Pay back into the laps of our neighbours seven times
Then we your people, the sheep of your pasture,
Hear us, Shepherd of Israel,
before Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasseh.
Restore us, O God;
How long, Lord God Almighty,
You have fed them with the bread of tears;
You have made us an object of derision to our neighbours,
Restore us, God Almighty;
You transplanted a vine from Egypt;
You cleared the ground for it,
The mountains were covered with its shade,
Its branches reached as far as the Sea,
Why have you broken down its walls
Boars from the forest ravage it,
Return to us, God Almighty!
the root your right hand has planted,
Your vine is cut down, it is burned with fire;
Let your hand rest on the man at your right hand,
Then we will not turn away from you;
Restore us, Lord God Almighty;
Sing for joy to God our strength;
Begin the music, strike the tambourine,
Sound the ram’s horn at the New Moon,
this is a decree for Israel,
When God went out against Egypt,
‘I removed the burden from their shoulders;
In your distress you called and I rescued you,
Hear me, my people, and I will warn you –
You shall have no foreign god among you;
I am the Lord your God,
‘But my people would not listen to me;
So I gave them over to their stubborn hearts
‘If my people would only listen to me,
how quickly I would subdue their enemies
Those who hate the Lord would cringe before him,
But you would be fed with the finest of wheat;
God presides in the great assembly;
‘How long will you defend the unjust
Defend the weak and the fatherless;
Rescue the weak and the needy;
‘The “gods” know nothing, they understand nothing.
‘I said, “You are ‘gods’;
But you will die like mere mortals;
Rise up, O God, judge the earth,
O God, do not remain silent;
See how your enemies growl,
With cunning they conspire against your people;
‘Come,’ they say, ‘let us destroy them as a nation,
With one mind they plot together;
the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites,
Byblos, Ammon and Amalek,
Even Assyria has joined them
Do to them as you did to Midian,
who perished at Endor
Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb,
who said, ‘Let us take possession
Make them like tumble-weed, my God,
As fire consumes the forest
so pursue them with your tempest
Cover their faces with shame, Lord,
May they ever be ashamed and dismayed;
Let them know that you, whose name is the Lord –
How lovely is your dwelling-place,
My soul yearns, even faints,
Even the sparrow has found a home,
Blessed are those who dwell in your house;
Blessed are those whose strength is in you,
As they pass through the Valley of Baka,
They go from strength to strength,
Hear my prayer, Lord God Almighty;
Look on our shield, O God;
Better is one day in your courts
For the Lord God is a sun and shield;
Lord Almighty,
You, Lord, showed favour to your land;
You forgave the iniquity of your people
You set aside all your wrath
Restore us again, God our Saviour,
Will you be angry with us for ever?
Will you not revive us again,
Show us your unfailing love, Lord,
I will listen to what God the Lord says;
Surely his salvation is near those who fear him,
Love and faithfulness meet together;
Faithfulness springs forth from the earth,
The Lord will indeed give what is good,
Righteousness goes before him
Hear me, Lord, and answer me,
Guard my life, for I am faithful to you;
have mercy on me, Lord,
Bring joy to your servant, Lord,
You, Lord, are forgiving and good,
Hear my prayer, Lord;
When I am in distress, I call to you,
Among the gods there is none like you, Lord;
All the nations you have made
For you are great and do marvellous deeds;
Teach me your way, Lord,
I will praise you, Lord my God, with all my heart;
For great is your love towards me;
Arrogant foes are attacking me, O God;
But you, Lord, are a compassionate and gracious God,
Turn to me and have mercy on me;
Give me a sign of your goodness,
He has founded his city on the holy mountain.
The Lord loves the gates of Zion
Glorious things are said of you,
‘I will record Rahab and Babylon
Indeed, of Zion it will be said,
The Lord will write in the register of the peoples:
As they make music they will sing,
Lord, you are the God who saves me;
May my prayer come before you;
I am overwhelmed with troubles
I am counted among those who go down to the pit;
I am set apart with the dead,
You have put me in the lowest pit,
Your wrath lies heavily on me;
You have taken from me my closest friends
my eyes are dim with grief.
Do you show your wonders to the dead?
Is your love declared in the grave,
Are your wonders known in the place of darkness,
But I cry to you for help, Lord;
Why, Lord, do you reject me
From my youth I have suffered and been close to death;
Your wrath has swept over me;
All day long they surround me like a flood;
You have taken from me friend and neighbour –
I will sing of the Lord’s great love for ever;
I will declare that your love stands firm for ever,
You said, ‘I have made a covenant with my chosen one,
“I will establish your line for ever
The heavens praise your wonders, Lord,
For who in the skies above can compare with the Lord?
In the council of the holy ones God is greatly feared;
Who is like you, Lord God Almighty?
You rule over the surging sea;
You crushed Rahab like one of the slain;
The heavens are yours, and yours also the earth;
You created the north and the south;
Your arm is endowed with power;
Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne;

If the Lord had not been on our side –
if the Lord had not been on our side
they would have swallowed us alive
the flood would have engulfed us,
the raging waters
Praise be to the Lord,
We have escaped like a bird
Our help is in the name of the Lord,
Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion,
As the mountains surround Jerusalem,
The sceptre of the wicked will not remain
Lord, do good to those who are good,
But those who turn to crooked ways
When the Lord restored the fortunes of Zion,
Our mouths were filled with laughter,
The Lord has done great things for us,
Restore our fortunes, Lord,
Those who sow with tears
Those who go out weeping,
Unless the Lord builds the house,
In vain you rise early
Children are a heritage from the Lord,
Like arrows in the hands of a warrior
Blessed is the man
Blessed are all who fear the Lord,
You will eat the fruit of your labour;
Your wife will be like a fruitful vine
Yes, this will be the blessing
May the Lord bless you from Zion;
May you live to see your children’s children –
‘They have greatly oppressed me from my youth,’
‘they have greatly oppressed me from my youth,
Ploughmen have ploughed my back
But the Lord is righteous;
May all who hate Zion
May they be like grass on the roof,
a reaper cannot fill his hands with it,
May those who pass by not say to them,
Out of the depths I cry to you, Lord;
Lord, hear my voice.
If you, Lord, kept a record of sins,
But with you there is forgiveness,
I wait for the Lord, my whole being waits,
I wait for the Lord
Israel, put your hope in the Lord,
He himself will redeem Israel
My heart is not proud, Lord,
But I have calmed and quietened myself,
Israel, put your hope in the Lord
Lord, remember David
He swore an oath to the Lord,
‘I will not enter my house
I will allow no sleep to my eyes
till I find a place for the Lord,
We heard it in Ephrathah,
‘Let us go to his dwelling-place,
“Arise, Lord, and come to your resting-place,
May your priests be clothed with your righteousness;
For the sake of your servant David,
The Lord swore an oath to David,
If your sons keep my covenant
For the Lord has chosen Zion,
‘This is my resting-place for ever and ever;
I will bless her with abundant provisions;
I will clothe her priests with salvation,
‘Here I will make a horn grow for David
I will clothe his enemies with shame,
How good and pleasant it is
It is like precious oil poured on the head,
It is as if the dew of Hermon
Praise the Lord, all you servants of the Lord
Lift up your hands in the sanctuary
May the Lord bless you from Zion,
Praise the Lord.
you who minister in the house of the Lord,
Praise the Lord, for the Lord is good;
For the Lord has chosen Jacob to be his own,
I know that the Lord is great,
The Lord does whatever pleases him,
He makes clouds rise from the ends of the earth;
He struck down the firstborn of Egypt,
He sent his signs and wonders into your midst, Egypt,
He struck down many nations
Sihon king of the Amorites,
and he gave their land as an inheritance,
Your name, Lord, endures for ever,
For the Lord will vindicate his people
The idols of the nations are silver and gold,
They have mouths, but cannot speak,
They have ears, but cannot hear,
Those who make them will be like them,
All you Israelites, praise the Lord;
house of Levi, praise the Lord;
Praise be to the Lord from Zion,
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good.
Give thanks to the God of gods.
Give thanks to the Lord of lords:
to him who alone does great wonders,
who by his understanding made the heavens,
who spread out the earth upon the waters,
who made the great lights –
the sun to govern the day,
the moon and stars to govern the night;
to him who struck down the firstborn of Egypt
and brought Israel out from among them
with a mighty hand and outstretched arm;
to him who divided the Red Sea asunder
and brought Israel through the midst of it,
but swept Pharaoh and his army into the Red Sea;
to him who led his people through the wilderness;
to him who struck down great kings,
and killed mighty kings –
Sihon king of the Amorites
and Og king of Bashan –
and gave their land as an inheritance,
an inheritance to his servant Israel.
He remembered us in our low estate
and freed us from our enemies.
He gives food to every creature.
Give thanks to the God of heaven.
By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept
There on the poplars
for there our captors asked us for songs,
How can we sing the songs of the Lord
If I forget you, Jerusalem,
May my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth
Remember, Lord, what the Edomites did
Daughter Babylon, doomed to destruction,
Happy is the one who seizes your infants
I will praise you, Lord, with all my heart;
I will bow down towards your holy temple
When I called, you answered me;
May all the kings of the earth praise you, Lord,
May they sing of the ways of the Lord,
Though the Lord is exalted, he looks kindly on the lowly;
Though I walk in the midst of trouble,
The Lord will vindicate me;
You have searched me, Lord,
You know when I sit and when I rise;
You discern my going out and my lying down;
Before a word is on my tongue
You hem me in behind and before,
Such knowledge is too wonderful for me,
Where can I go from your Spirit?
If I go up to the heavens, you are there;
If I rise on the wings of the dawn,
even there your hand will guide me,
If I say, ‘Surely the darkness will hide me
even the darkness will not be dark to you;
For you created my inmost being;
I praise you because I am fearfully and wonderfully made;
My frame was not hidden from you
Your eyes saw my unformed body;
How precious to me are your thoughts, God!
Were I to count them,
If only you, God, would slay the wicked!
They speak of you with evil intent;
Do I not hate those who hate you, Lord,
I have nothing but hatred for them;
Search me, God, and know my heart;
See if there is any offensive way in me,
Rescue me, Lord, from evildoers;
who devise evil plans in their hearts
They make their tongues as sharp as a serpent’s;
Keep me safe, Lord, from the hands of the wicked;
The arrogant have hidden a snare for me;
I say to the Lord, ‘You are my God.’
Sovereign Lord, my strong deliverer,
Do not grant the wicked their desires, Lord;
Those who surround me proudly rear their heads;
May burning coals fall on them;
May slanderers not be established in the land;
I know that the Lord secures justice for the poor
Surely the righteous will praise your name,
I call to you, Lord, come quickly to me;
May my prayer be set before you like incense;
Set a guard over my mouth, Lord;
Do not let my heart be drawn to what is evil
Let a righteous man strike me – that is a kindness;
Their rulers will be thrown down from the cliffs,
They will say, ‘As one ploughs and breaks up the earth,
But my eyes are fixed on you, Sovereign Lord;
Keep me safe from the traps set by evildoers,
Let the wicked fall into their own nets,
I cry aloud to the Lord;
I pour out before him my complaint;
When my spirit grows faint within me,
Look and see, there is no-one at my right hand;
I cry to you, Lord;
Listen to my cry,
Set me free from my prison,
Lord, hear my prayer,
Do not bring your servant into judgment,
The enemy pursues me,
So my spirit grows faint within me;
I remember the days of long ago;
I spread out my hands to you;
Answer me quickly, Lord;
Let the morning bring me word of your unfailing love,
Rescue me from my enemies, Lord,
Teach me to do your will,
For your name’s sake, Lord, preserve my life;
In your unfailing love, silence my enemies;
Praise be to the Lord my Rock,
He is my loving God and my fortress,
Lord, what are human beings that you care for them,
They are like a breath;
Part your heavens, Lord, and come down;
Send forth lightning and scatter the enemy;
Reach down your hand from on high;
whose mouths are full of lies,
I will sing a new song to you, my God;
to the One who gives victory to kings,
deliver me;
Then our sons in their youth
Our barns will be filled
our oxen will draw heavy loads.
Blessed is the people of whom this is true;
I will exalt you, my God the King;
Every day I will praise you
Great is the Lord and most worthy of praise;
One generation commends your works to another;
They speak of the glorious splendour of your majesty –
They tell of the power of your awesome works –
They celebrate your abundant goodness
The Lord is gracious and compassionate,
The Lord is good to all;
All your works praise you, Lord;
They tell of the glory of your kingdom
so that all people may know of your mighty acts
Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom,
The Lord upholds all who fall
The eyes of all look to you,
You open your hand
The Lord is righteous in all his ways
The Lord is near to all who call on him,
He fulfils the desires of those who fear him;
The Lord watches over all who love him,
My mouth will speak in praise of the Lord.
Praise the Lord.
I will praise the Lord all my life;
Do not put your trust in princes,
When their spirit departs, they return to the ground;
Blessed are those whose help is the God of Jacob,
He is the Maker of heaven and earth,
He upholds the cause of the oppressed
the Lord gives sight to the blind,
The Lord watches over the foreigner
The Lord reigns for ever,
Praise the Lord.
The Lord builds up Jerusalem;
He heals the broken-hearted
He determines the number of the stars
Great is our Lord and mighty in power;
The Lord sustains the humble
Sing to the Lord with grateful praise;
He covers the sky with clouds;
He provides food for the cattle
His pleasure is not in the strength of the horse,
the Lord delights in those who fear him,
Extol the Lord, Jerusalem;
He strengthens the bars of your gates
He grants peace to your borders
He sends his command to the earth;
He spreads the snow like wool
He hurls down hail like pebbles.
He sends his word and melts them;
He has revealed his word to Jacob,
He has done this for no other nation;
Praise the Lord.
Praise him, all his angels;
Praise him, sun and moon;
Praise him, you highest heavens
Let them praise the name of the Lord,
and he established them for ever and ever –
Praise the Lord from the earth,
lightning and hail, snow and clouds,
you mountains and all hills,
wild animals and all cattle,
kings of the earth and all nations,
young men and women,
Let them praise the name of the Lord,
And he has raised up for his people a horn,
Praise the Lord.
Let Israel rejoice in their Maker;
Let them praise his name with dancing
For the Lord takes delight in his people;
Let his faithful people rejoice in this honour
May the praise of God be in their mouths
to inflict vengeance on the nations
to bind their kings with fetters,
to carry out the sentence written against them –
Praise the Lord.
Praise him for his acts of power;
Praise him with the sounding of the trumpet,
praise him with tambourine and dancing,
praise him with the clash of cymbals,
Let everything that has breath praise the Lord.
The proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel:
for gaining wisdom and instruction;
for receiving instruction in prudent behaviour,
for giving prudence to those who are simple,
let the wise listen and add to their learning,
for understanding proverbs and parables,
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge,
Listen, my son, to your father’s instruction
They are a garland to grace your head
My son, if sinful men entice you,
If they say, ‘Come along with us;
let’s swallow them alive, like the grave,
we will get all sorts of valuable things
cast lots with us;
my son, do not go along with them,
for their feet rush into evil,
How useless to spread a net
These men lie in wait for their own blood;
Such are the paths of all who go after ill-gotten gain;
Out in the open wisdom calls aloud,
on top of the wall she cries out,
‘How long will you who are simple love your simple ways?
Repent at my rebuke!
But since you refuse to listen when I call
since you disregard all my advice
I in turn will laugh when disaster strikes you;
when calamity overtakes you like a storm,
‘Then they will call to me but I will not answer;
since they hated knowledge
Since they would not accept my advice
they will eat the fruit of their ways
For the waywardness of the simple will kill them,
but whoever listens to me will live in safety
My son, if you accept my words
turning your ear to wisdom
indeed, if you call out for insight
and if you look for it as for silver
then you will understand the fear of the Lord
For the Lord gives wisdom;
He holds success in store for the upright,
for he guards the course of the just
Then you will understand what is right and just
For wisdom will enter your heart,
Discretion will protect you,
Wisdom will save you from the ways of wicked men,
who have left the straight paths
who delight in doing wrong
whose paths are crooked
Wisdom will save you also from the adulterous woman,
who has left the partner of her youth
Surely her house leads down to death
None who go to her return
Thus you will walk in the ways of the good
For the upright will live in the land,
but the wicked will be cut off from the land,
My son, do not forget my teaching,
for they will prolong your life many years
Let love and faithfulness never leave you;
Then you will win favour and a good name
Trust in the Lord with all your heart
in all your ways submit to him,
Do not be wise in your own eyes;
This will bring health to your body
Honour the Lord with your wealth,
then your barns will be filled to overflowing,
My son, do not despise the Lord’s discipline,
because the Lord disciplines those he loves,
Blessed are those who find wisdom,
for she is more profitable than silver
She is more precious than rubies;
Long life is in her right hand;
Her ways are pleasant ways,
She is a tree of life to those who take hold of her;
By wisdom the Lord laid the earth’s foundations,
by his knowledge the watery depths were divided,
My son, do not let wisdom and understanding out of your sight,
they will be life for you,
Then you will go on your way in safety,
When you lie down, you will not be afraid;
Have no fear of sudden disaster
for the Lord will be at your side
Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due,
Do not say to your neighbour,
Do not plot harm against your neighbour,
Do not accuse anyone for no reason –
Do not envy the violent
For the Lord detests the perverse
The Lord’s curse is on the house of the wicked,
He mocks proud mockers
The wise inherit honour,
Listen, my sons, to a father’s instruction;
I give you sound learning,
For I too was a son to my father,
Then he taught me, and he said to me,
Get wisdom, get understanding;
Do not forsake wisdom, and she will protect you;
The beginning of wisdom is this: get wisdom.
Cherish her, and she will exalt you;
She will give you a garland to grace your head
Listen, my son, accept what I say,
I instruct you in the way of wisdom
When you walk, your steps will not be hampered;
Hold on to instruction, do not let it go;
Do not set foot on the path of the wicked
Avoid it, do not travel on it;
For they cannot rest until they do evil;
They eat the bread of wickedness
The path of the righteous is like the morning sun,
But the way of the wicked is like deep darkness;
My son, pay attention to what I say;
Do not let them out of your sight,
for they are life to those who find them
Above all else, guard your heart,
Keep your mouth free of perversity;
Let your eyes look straight ahead;
Give careful thought to the paths for your feet
Do not turn to the right or the left;
My son, pay attention to my wisdom,
that you may maintain discretion
For the lips of the adulterous woman drip honey,
but in the end she is bitter as gall,
Her feet go down to death;
She gives no thought to the way of life;
Now then, my sons, listen to me;
Keep to a path far from her,
lest you lose your honour to others
lest strangers feast on your wealth
At the end of your life you will groan,
You will say, ‘How I hated discipline!
I would not obey my teachers
And I was soon in serious trouble
Drink water from your own cistern,
Should your springs overflow in the streets,
Let them be yours alone,
May your fountain be blessed,
A loving doe, a graceful deer –
Why, my son, be intoxicated with another man’s wife?
For your ways are in full view of the Lord,
The evil deeds of the wicked ensnare them;
For lack of discipline they will die,
My son, if you have put up security for your neighbour,
you have been trapped by what you said,
So do this, my son, to free yourself,
Allow no sleep to your eyes,
Free yourself, like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter,
Go to the ant, you sluggard;
It has no commander,
yet it stores its provisions in summer
How long will you lie there, you sluggard?
A little sleep, a little slumber,
and poverty will come on you like a thief
A troublemaker and a villain,
who winks maliciously with his eye,
who plots evil with deceit in his heart –
Therefore disaster will overtake him in an instant;
There are six things the Lord hates,
haughty eyes,
a heart that devises wicked schemes,
a false witness who pours out lies
My son, keep your father’s command
Bind them always on your heart;
When you walk, they will guide you;
For this command is a lamp,
keeping you from your neighbour’s wife,
Do not lust in your heart after her beauty
For a prostitute can be had for a loaf of bread,
Can a man scoop fire into his lap
Can a man walk on hot coals
So is he who sleeps with another man’s wife;
People do not despise a thief if he steals
Yet if he is caught, he must pay sevenfold,
But a man who commits adultery has no sense;
Blows and disgrace are his lot,
For jealousy arouses a husband’s fury,
He will not accept any compensation;
My son, keep my words
Keep my commands and you will live;
Bind them on your fingers;
Say to wisdom, ‘You are my sister,’
They will keep you from the adulterous woman,
At the window of my house
I saw among the simple,
He was going down the street near her corner,
at twilight, as the day was fading,
Then out came a woman to meet him,
(She is unruly and defiant,
now in the street, now in the squares,
She took hold of him and kissed him
‘Today I fulfilled my vows,
So I came out to meet you;
I have covered my bed
I have perfumed my bed
Come, let’s drink deeply of love till morning;
My husband is not at home;
He took his purse filled with money
With persuasive words she led him astray;
All at once he followed her
till an arrow pierces his liver,
Now then, my sons, listen to me;
Do not let your heart turn to her ways
Many are the victims she has brought down;
Her house is a highway to the grave,
Does not wisdom call out?
At the highest point along the way,
beside the gate leading into the city,
‘To you, O people, I call out;
You who are simple, gain prudence;
Listen, for I have trustworthy things to say;
My mouth speaks what is true,
All the words of my mouth are just;
To the discerning all of them are right;
Choose my instruction instead of silver,
for wisdom is more precious than rubies,
‘I, wisdom, dwell together with prudence;
To fear the Lord is to hate evil;
Counsel and sound judgment are mine;
By me kings reign
by me princes govern,
I love those who love me,
With me are riches and honour,
My fruit is better than fine gold;
I walk in the way of righteousness,
bestowing a rich inheritance on those who love me
‘The Lord brought me forth as the first of his works,
I was formed long ages ago,
When there were no watery depths, I was given birth,
before the mountains were settled in place,
before he made the world or its fields
I was there when he set the heavens in place,
when he established the clouds above
when he gave the sea its boundary
Then I was constantly at his side.
rejoicing in his whole world
‘Now then, my children, listen to me;
Listen to my instruction and be wise;
Blessed are those who listen to me,
For those who find me find life
But those who fail to find me harm themselves;
Wisdom has built her house;
She has prepared her meat and mixed her wine;
She has sent out her servants, and she calls
‘Let all who are simple come to my house!’
‘Come, eat my food
Leave your simple ways and you will live;
Whoever corrects a mocker invites insults;
Do not rebuke mockers or they will hate you;
Instruct the wise and they will be wiser still;
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom,
For through wisdom your days will be many,
If you are wise, your wisdom will reward you;
Folly is an unruly woman;
She sits at the door of her house,
calling out to those who pass by,
‘Let all who are simple come to my house!’
‘Stolen water is sweet;
But little do they know that the dead are there,
The proverbs of Solomon:
Ill-gotten treasures have no lasting value,
The Lord does not let the righteous go hungry,
Lazy hands make for poverty,
He who gathers crops in summer is a prudent son,
Blessings crown the head of the righteous,
The name of the righteous is used in blessings,
The wise in heart accept commands,
Whoever walks in integrity walks securely,
Whoever winks maliciously causes grief,
The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life,
Hatred stirs up conflict,
Wisdom is found on the lips of the discerning,
The wise store up knowledge,
The wealth of the rich is their fortified city,
The wages of the righteous is life,
Whoever heeds discipline shows the way to life,
Whoever conceals hatred with lying lips
Sin is not ended by multiplying words,
The tongue of the righteous is choice silver,
The lips of the righteous nourish many,
The blessing of the Lord brings wealth,
A fool finds pleasure in wicked schemes,
What the wicked dread will overtake them;
When the storm has swept by, the wicked are gone,
As vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes,
The fear of the Lord adds length to life,
The prospect of the righteous is joy,
The way of the Lord is a refuge for the blameless,
The righteous will never be uprooted,
From the mouth of the righteous comes the fruit of wisdom,
The lips of the righteous know what finds favour,
The Lord detests dishonest scales,
When pride comes, then comes disgrace,
The integrity of the upright guides them,
Wealth is worthless in the day of wrath,
The righteousness of the blameless makes their paths straight,
The righteousness of the upright delivers them,
Hopes placed in mortals die with them;
The righteous person is rescued from trouble,
With their mouths the godless destroy their neighbours,
When the righteous prosper, the city rejoices;
Through the blessing of the upright a city is exalted,
Whoever derides their neighbour has no sense,
A gossip betrays a confidence,
For lack of guidance a nation falls,
Whoever puts up security for a stranger will surely suffer,
A kind-hearted woman gains honour,
Those who are kind benefit themselves,
A wicked person earns deceptive wages,
Truly the righteous attain life,
The Lord detests those whose hearts are perverse,
Be sure of this: the wicked will not go unpunished,
Like a gold ring in a pig’s snout
The desire of the righteous ends only in good,
One person gives freely, yet gains even more;
A generous person will prosper;
People curse the one who hoards grain,
Whoever seeks good finds favour,
Those who trust in their riches will fall,
Whoever brings ruin on their family will inherit only wind,
The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life,
If the righteous receive their due on earth,
Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge,
Good people obtain favour from the Lord,
No-one can be established through wickedness,
A wife of noble character is her husband’s crown,
The plans of the righteous are just,
The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood,
The wicked are overthrown and are no more,
A person is praised according to their prudence,
Better to be a nobody and yet have a servant
The righteous care for the needs of their animals,
Those who work their land will have abundant food,
The wicked desire the stronghold of evildoers,
Evildoers are trapped by their sinful talk,
From the fruit of their lips people are filled with good things,
The way of fools seems right to them,
Fools show their annoyance at once,
An honest witness tells the truth,
The words of the reckless pierce like swords,
Truthful lips endure for ever,
Deceit is in the hearts of those who plot evil,
No harm overtakes the righteous,
The Lord detests lying lips,
The prudent keep their knowledge to themselves,
Diligent hands will rule,
Anxiety weighs down the heart,
The righteous choose their friends carefully,
The lazy do not roast any game,
In the way of righteousness there is life;
A wise son heeds his father’s instruction,
From the fruit of their lips people enjoy good things,
Those who guard their lips preserve their lives,
A sluggard’s appetite is never filled,
The righteous hate what is false,
Righteousness guards the person of integrity,
One person pretends to be rich, yet has nothing;
A person’s riches may ransom their life,
The light of the righteous shines brightly,
Where there is strife, there is pride,
Dishonest money dwindles away,
Hope deferred makes the heart sick,
Whoever scorns instruction will pay for it,
The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life,
Good judgment wins favour,
All who are prudent act with knowledge,
A wicked messenger falls into trouble,
Whoever disregards discipline comes to poverty and shame,
A longing fulfilled is sweet to the soul,
Walk with the wise and become wise,
Trouble pursues the sinner,
A good person leaves an inheritance for their children’s children,
An unploughed field produces food for the poor,
Whoever spares the rod hates their children,
The righteous eat to their hearts’ content,
The wise woman builds her house,
Whoever fears the Lord walks uprightly,
A fool’s mouth lashes out with pride,
Where there are no oxen, the manger is empty,
An honest witness does not deceive,
The mocker seeks wisdom and finds none,
Stay away from a fool,
The wisdom of the prudent is to give thought to their ways,
Fools mock at making amends for sin,
Each heart knows its own bitterness,
The house of the wicked will be destroyed,
There is a way that appears to be right,
Even in laughter the heart may ache,
The faithless will be fully repaid for their ways,
The simple believe anything,
The wise fear the Lord and shun evil,
A quick-tempered person does foolish things,
The simple inherit folly,
Evildoers will bow down in the presence of the good,
The poor are shunned even by their neighbours,
It is a sin to despise one’s neighbour,
Do not those who plot evil go astray?
All hard work brings a profit,
The wealth of the wise is their crown,
A truthful witness saves lives,
Whoever fears the Lord has a secure fortress,
The fear of the Lord is a fountain of life,
A large population is a king’s glory,
Whoever is patient has great understanding,
A heart at peace gives life to the body,
Whoever oppresses the poor shows contempt for their Maker,
When calamity comes, the wicked are brought down,
Wisdom reposes in the heart of the discerning
Righteousness exalts a nation,
A king delights in a wise servant,
A gentle answer turns away wrath,
The tongue of the wise adorns knowledge,
The eyes of the Lord are everywhere,
The soothing tongue is a tree of life,
A fool spurns a parent’s discipline,
The house of the righteous contains great treasure,
The lips of the wise spread knowledge,
The Lord detests the sacrifice of the wicked,
The Lord detests the way of the wicked,
Stern discipline awaits anyone who leaves the path;
Death and Destruction lie open before the Lord –
Mockers resent correction,
A happy heart makes the face cheerful,
The discerning heart seeks knowledge,
All the days of the oppressed are wretched,
Better a little with the fear of the Lord
Better a dish of vegetables with love
A hot-tempered person stirs up conflict,
The way of the sluggard is blocked with thorns,
A wise son brings joy to his father,
Folly brings joy to one who has no sense,
Plans fail for lack of counsel,
A person finds joy in giving an apt reply –
The path of life leads upward for the prudent
The Lord tears down the house of the proud,
The Lord detests the thoughts of the wicked,
The greedy bring ruin to their households,
The heart of the righteous weighs its answers,
The Lord is far from the wicked,
Light in a messenger’s eyes brings joy to the heart,
Whoever heeds life-giving correction
Those who disregard discipline despise themselves,
Wisdom’s instruction is to fear the Lord,
To humans belong the plans of the heart,
All a person’s ways seem pure to them,
Commit to the Lord whatever you do,
The Lord works out everything to its proper end –
The Lord detests all the proud of heart.
Through love and faithfulness sin is atoned for;
When the Lord takes pleasure in anyone’s way,
Better a little with righteousness
In their hearts humans plan their course,
The lips of a king speak as an oracle,
Honest scales and balances belong to the Lord;
Kings detest wrongdoing,
Kings take pleasure in honest lips;
A king’s wrath is a messenger of death,
When a king’s face brightens, it means life;
How much better to get wisdom than gold,
The highway of the upright avoids evil;
Pride goes before destruction,
Better to be lowly in spirit along with the oppressed
Whoever gives heed to instruction prospers,
The wise in heart are called discerning,
Prudence is a fountain of life to the prudent,
The hearts of the wise make their mouths prudent,
Gracious words are a honeycomb,
There is a way that appears to be right,
The appetite of labourers works for them;
A scoundrel plots evil,
A perverse person stirs up conflict,
A violent person entices their neighbour
Whoever winks with their eye is plotting perversity;
Grey hair is a crown of splendour;
Better a patient person than a warrior,
The lot is cast into the lap,
Better a dry crust with peace and quiet
A prudent servant will rule over a disgraceful son
The crucible for silver and the furnace for gold,
A wicked person listens to deceitful lips;
Whoever mocks the poor shows contempt for their Maker;
Children’s children are a crown to the aged,
Eloquent lips are unsuited to a godless fool –
A bribe is seen as a charm by the one who gives it;
Whoever would foster love covers over an offence,
A rebuke impresses a discerning person
Evildoers foster rebellion against God;
Better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs
Evil will never leave the house
Starting a quarrel is like breaching a dam;
Acquitting the guilty and condemning the innocent –
Why should fools have money in hand to buy wisdom,
A friend loves at all times,
One who has no sense shakes hands in pledge
Whoever loves a quarrel loves sin;
One whose heart is corrupt does not prosper;
To have a fool for a child brings grief;
A cheerful heart is good medicine,
The wicked accept bribes in secret
A discerning person keeps wisdom in view,
A foolish son brings grief to his father
If imposing a fine on the innocent is not good,
The one who has knowledge uses words with restraint,
Even fools are thought wise if they keep silent,
An unfriendly person pursues selfish ends
Fools find no pleasure in understanding
When wickedness comes, so does contempt,
The words of the mouth are deep waters,
It is not good to be partial to the wicked
The lips of fools bring them strife,
The mouths of fools are their undoing,
The words of a gossip are like choice morsels;
One who is slack in his work
The name of the Lord is a fortified tower;
The wealth of the rich is their fortified city;
Before a downfall the heart is haughty,
To answer before listening –
The human spirit can endure in times of illness,
The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge,
A gift opens the way
In a lawsuit the first to speak seems right,
Casting the lot settles disputes
A brother wronged is more unyielding than a fortified city;
From the fruit of their mouth a person’s stomach is filled;
The tongue has the power of life and death,
He who finds a wife finds what is good
The poor plead for mercy,
One who has unreliable friends soon comes to ruin,
Better the poor whose way of life is blameless
Desire without knowledge is not good –
A person’s own folly leads to their ruin,
Wealth attracts many friends,
A false witness will not go unpunished,
Many curry favour with a ruler,
The poor are shunned by all their relatives –
The one who gets wisdom loves life;
A false witness will not go unpunished,
It is not fitting for a fool to live in luxury –
A person’s wisdom yields patience;
A king’s rage is like the roar of a lion,
A foolish child is a father’s ruin,
Houses and wealth are inherited from parents,
Laziness brings on deep sleep,
Whoever keeps commandments keeps their life,
Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the Lord,
Discipline your children, for in that there is hope;
A hot-tempered person must pay the penalty;
Listen to advice and accept discipline,
Many are the plans in a person’s heart,
What a person desires is unfailing love;
The fear of the Lord leads to life;
A sluggard buries his hand in the dish;
Flog a mocker, and the simple will learn prudence;
Whoever robs their father and drives out their mother
Stop listening to instruction, my son,
A corrupt witness mocks at justice,
Penalties are prepared for mockers,
Wine is a mocker and beer a brawler;
A king’s wrath strikes terror like the roar of a lion;
It is to one’s honour to avoid strife,
Sluggards do not plough in season;
The purposes of a person’s heart are deep waters,
Many claim to have unfailing love,
The righteous lead blameless lives;
When a king sits on his throne to judge,
Who can say, ‘I have kept my heart pure;
Differing weights and differing measures –
Even small children are known by their actions,
Ears that hear and eyes that see –
Do not love sleep or you will grow poor;
‘It’s no good, it’s no good!’ says the buyer –
Gold there is, and rubies in abundance,
Take the garment of one who puts up security for a stranger;
Food gained by fraud tastes sweet,
Plans are established by seeking advice;
A gossip betrays a confidence;
If someone curses their father or mother,
An inheritance claimed too soon
Do not say, ‘I’ll pay you back for this wrong!’
The Lord detests differing weights,
A person’s steps are directed by the Lord.
It is a trap to dedicate something rashly
A wise king winnows out the wicked;
The human spirit is the lamp of the Lord
Love and faithfulness keep a king safe;
The glory of young men is their strength,
Blows and wounds scrub away evil,
In the Lord’s hand the king’s heart is a stream of water
A person may think their own ways are right,
To do what is right and just
Haughty eyes and a proud heart –
The plans of the diligent lead to profit
A fortune made by a lying tongue
The violence of the wicked will drag them away,
The way of the guilty is devious,
Better to live on a corner of the roof
The wicked crave evil;
When a mocker is punished, the simple gain wisdom;
The Righteous One takes note of the house of the wicked
Whoever shuts their ears to the cry of the poor
A gift given in secret soothes anger,
When justice is done, it brings joy to the righteous
Whoever strays from the path of prudence
Whoever loves pleasure will become poor;
The wicked become a ransom for the righteous,
Better to live in a desert
The wise store up choice food and olive oil,
Whoever pursues righteousness and love
One who is wise can go up against the city of the mighty
Those who guard their mouths and their tongues
The proud and arrogant person – ‘Mocker’ is his name –
The craving of a sluggard will be the death of him,
All day long he craves for more,
The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable –
A false witness will perish,
The wicked put up a bold front,
There is no wisdom, no insight, no plan
The horse is made ready for the day of battle,
A good name is more desirable than great riches;
Rich and poor have this in common:
The prudent see danger and take refuge,
Humility is the fear of the Lord;
In the paths of the wicked are snares and pitfalls,
Start children off on the way they should go,
The rich rule over the poor,
Whoever sows injustice reaps calamity,
The generous will themselves be blessed,
Drive out the mocker, and out goes strife;
One who loves a pure heart and who speaks with grace
The eyes of the Lord keep watch over knowledge,
The sluggard says, ‘There’s a lion outside!
The mouth of an adulterous woman is a deep pit;
Folly is bound up in the heart of a child,
One who oppresses the poor to increase his wealth
Pay attention and turn your ear to the sayings of the wise;
for it is pleasing when you keep them in your heart
So that your trust may be in the Lord,
Have I not written thirty sayings for you,
teaching you to be honest and to speak the truth,
Do not exploit the poor because they are poor
for the Lord will take up their case
Do not make friends with a hot-tempered person,
or you may learn their ways
Do not be one who shakes hands in pledge
if you lack the means to pay,
Do not move an ancient boundary stone
Do you see someone skilled in their work?
When you sit to dine with a ruler,
and put a knife to your throat
Do not crave his delicacies,
Do not wear yourself out to get rich;
Cast but a glance at riches, and they are gone,
Do not eat the food of a stingy host,
for he is the kind of person
You will vomit up the little you have eaten
Do not speak to fools,
Do not move an ancient boundary stone
for their Defender is strong;
Apply your heart to instruction
Do not withhold discipline from a child;
Punish them with the rod
My son, if your heart is wise,
my inmost being will rejoice
Do not let your heart envy sinners,
There is surely a future hope for you,
Listen, my son, and be wise,
do not join those who drink too much wine
for drunkards and gluttons become poor,
Listen to your father, who gave you life,
Buy the truth and do not sell it –
The father of a righteous child has great joy;
May your father and mother rejoice;
My son, give me your heart
for an adulterous woman is a deep pit,
Like a bandit she lies in wait
Who has woe? Who has sorrow?
Those who linger over wine,
Do not gaze at wine when it is red,
In the end it bites like a snake
Your eyes will see strange sights,
You will be like one sleeping on the high seas,
‘They hit me,’ you will say, ‘but I’m not hurt!
Do not envy the wicked,
for their hearts plot violence,
By wisdom a house is built,
through knowledge its rooms are filled
The wise prevail through great power,
Surely you need guidance to wage war,
Wisdom is too high for fools;
Whoever plots evil
The schemes of folly are sin,
If you falter in a time of trouble,
Rescue those being led away to death;
If you say, ‘But we knew nothing about this,’
Eat honey, my son, for it is good;
Know also that wisdom is like honey for you:
Do not lurk like a thief near the house of the righteous,
for though the righteous fall seven times, they rise again,
Do not gloat when your enemy falls;
or the Lord will see and disapprove
Do not fret because of evildoers
for the evildoer has no future hope,
Fear the Lord and the king, my son,
for those two will send sudden destruction on them,
These also are sayings of the wise:
whoever says to the guilty, ‘You are innocent,’
But it will go well with those who convict the guilty,
An honest answer
Put your outdoor work in order
Do not testify against your neighbour without cause –
Do not say, ‘I’ll do to them as they have done to me;
I went past the field of a sluggard,
thorns had come up everywhere,
I applied my heart to what I observed
a little sleep, a little slumber,
and poverty will come on you like a thief
These are more proverbs of Solomon, compiled by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah:
It is the glory of God to conceal a matter;
As the heavens are high and the earth is deep,
Remove the dross from the silver,
remove wicked officials from the king’s presence,
Do not exalt yourself in the king’s presence,
it is better for him to say to you, ‘Come up here,’
do not bring hastily to court,
If you take your neighbour to court,
or the one who hears it may shame you
Like apples of gold in settings of silver
Like an earring of gold or an ornament of fine gold
Like a snow-cooled drink at harvest time
Like clouds and wind without rain
Through patience a ruler can be persuaded,
If you find honey, eat just enough –
Seldom set foot in your neighbour’s house –
Like a club or a sword or a sharp arrow
Like a broken tooth or a lame foot
Like one who takes away a garment on a cold day,
If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat;
In doing this, you will heap burning coals on his head,
Like a north wind that brings unexpected rain
Better to live on a corner of the roof
Like cold water to a weary soul
Like a muddied spring or a polluted well
It is not good to eat too much honey,
Like a city whose walls are broken through
Like snow in summer or rain in harvest,
Like a fluttering sparrow or a darting swallow,
A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey,
Do not answer a fool according to his folly,
Answer a fool according to his folly,
Sending a message by the hands of a fool
Like the useless legs of one who is lame
Like tying a stone in a sling
Like a thorn-bush in a drunkard’s hand
Like an archer who wounds at random
As a dog returns to its vomit,
Do you see a person wise in their own eyes?
A sluggard says, ‘There’s a lion in the road,
As a door turns on its hinges,
A sluggard buries his hand in the dish;
A sluggard is wiser in his own eyes
Like one who grabs a stray dog by the ears
Like a maniac shooting
is one who deceives their neighbour
Without wood a fire goes out;
As charcoal to embers and as wood to fire,
The words of a gossip are like choice morsels;
Like a coating of silver dross on earthenware
Enemies disguise themselves with their lips,
Though their speech is charming, do not believe them,
Their malice may be concealed by deception,
Whoever digs a pit will fall into it;
A lying tongue hates those it hurts,
Do not boast about tomorrow,
Let someone else praise you, and not your own mouth;
Stone is heavy and sand a burden,
Anger is cruel and fury overwhelming,
Better is open rebuke
Wounds from a friend can be trusted,
One who is full loathes honey from the comb,
Like a bird that flees its nest
Perfume and incense bring joy to the heart,
Do not forsake your friend or a friend of your family,
Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart;
The prudent see danger and take refuge,
Take the garment of one who puts up security for a stranger;
If anyone loudly blesses their neighbour early in the morning,
A quarrelsome wife is like the dripping
restraining her is like restraining the wind
As iron sharpens iron,
The one who guards a fig-tree will eat its fruit,
As water reflects the face,
Death and Destruction are never satisfied,
The crucible for silver and the furnace for gold,
Though you grind a fool in a mortar,
Be sure you know the condition of your flocks,
for riches do not endure for ever,
When the hay is removed and new growth appears
the lambs will provide you with clothing,
You will have plenty of goats’ milk to feed your family
The wicked flee though no-one pursues,
When a country is rebellious, it has many rulers,
A ruler who oppresses the poor
Those who forsake instruction praise the wicked,
Evildoers do not understand what is right,
Better the poor whose way of life is blameless
A discerning son heeds instruction,
Whoever increases wealth by taking interest or profit from the poor
If anyone turns a deaf ear to my instruction,
Whoever leads the upright along an evil path
The rich are wise in their own eyes;
When the righteous triumph, there is great elation;
Whoever conceals their sins does not prosper,
Blessed is the one who always trembles before God,
Like a roaring lion or a charging bear
A tyrannical ruler practises extortion,
Anyone tormented by the guilt of murder
The one whose way of life is blameless is kept safe,
Those who work their land will have abundant food,
A faithful person will be richly blessed,
To show partiality is not good –
The stingy are eager to get rich
Whoever rebukes a person will in the end gain favour
Whoever robs their father or mother
The greedy stir up conflict,
Those who trust in themselves are fools,
Those who give to the poor will lack nothing,
When the wicked rise to power, people go into hiding;
Whoever remains stiff-necked after many rebukes
When the righteous thrive, the people rejoice;
A man who loves wisdom brings joy to his father,
By justice a king gives a country stability,
Those who flatter their neighbours
Evildoers are snared by their own sin,
The righteous care about justice for the poor,
Mockers stir up a city,
If a wise person goes to court with a fool,
The bloodthirsty hate a person of integrity
Fools give full vent to their rage,
If a ruler listens to lies,
The poor and the oppressor have this in common:
If a king judges the poor with fairness,
A rod and a reprimand impart wisdom,
When the wicked thrive, so does sin,
Discipline your children, and they will give you peace;
Where there is no revelation, people cast off restraint;
Servants cannot be corrected by mere words;
Do you see someone who speaks in haste?
A servant pampered from youth
An angry person stirs up conflict,
Pride brings a person low,
The accomplices of thieves are their own enemies;
Fear of man will prove to be a snare,
Many seek an audience with a ruler,
The righteous detest the dishonest;
The sayings of Agur son of Jakeh – an inspired utterance.
Surely I am only a brute, not a man;
I have not learned wisdom,
Who has gone up to heaven and come down?
‘Every word of God is flawless;
Do not add to his words,
‘Two things I ask of you, Lord;
keep falsehood and lies far from me;
Otherwise, I may have too much and disown you
‘Do not slander a servant to their master,
‘There are those who curse their fathers
those who are pure in their own eyes
those whose eyes are ever so haughty,
those whose teeth are swords
‘The leech has two daughters.
the grave
‘The eye that mocks a father,
‘There are three things that are too amazing for me,
the way of an eagle in the sky,
‘This is the way of an adulterous woman:
‘Under three things the earth trembles,
a servant who becomes king,
a contemptible woman who gets married,
‘Four things on earth are small,
ants are creatures of little strength,
hyraxes are creatures of little power,
locusts have no king,
a lizard can be caught with the hand,
‘There are three things that are stately in their stride,
a lion, mighty among beasts, who retreats before nothing;
a strutting cock,
‘If you play the fool and exalt yourself,
For as churning cream produces butter,
The sayings of King Lemuel – an inspired utterance his mother taught him.
Listen, my son! Listen, son of my womb!
Do not spend your strength on women,
It is not for kings, Lemuel –
lest they drink and forget what has been decreed,
Let beer be for those who are perishing,
Let them drink and forget their poverty
Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves,
Speak up and judge fairly;
A wife of noble character who can find?
Her husband has full confidence in her
She brings him good, not harm,
She selects wool and flax
She is like the merchant ships,
She gets up while it is still night;
She considers a field and buys it;
She sets about her work vigorously;
She sees that her trading is profitable,
In her hand she holds the distaff
She opens her arms to the poor
When it snows, she has no fear for her household;
She makes coverings for her bed;
Her husband is respected at the city gate,
She makes linen garments and sells them,
She is clothed with strength and dignity;
She speaks with wisdom,
She watches over the affairs of her household
Her children arise and call her blessed;
‘Many women do noble things,
Charm is deceptive, and beauty is fleeting;
Honour her for all that her hands have done,
The words of the Teacher, son of David, king of Jerusalem:
‘Meaningless! Meaningless!’
What do people gain from all their labours
Generations come and generations go,
The sun rises and the sun sets,
The wind blows to the south
All streams flow into the sea,
All things are wearisome,
What has been will be again,
Is there anything of which one can say,
No-one remembers the former generations,
I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
I applied my mind to study and to explore by wisdom all that is done under the heavens. What a heavy burden God has laid on mankind!
I have seen all the things that are done under the sun; all of them are meaningless, a chasing after the wind.
What is crooked cannot be straightened;
I said to myself, ‘Look, I have increased in wisdom more than anyone who has ruled over Jerusalem before me; I have experienced much of wisdom and knowledge.’
Then I applied myself to the understanding of wisdom, and also of madness and folly, but I learned that this, too, is a chasing after the wind.
For with much wisdom comes much sorrow;
I said to myself, ‘Come now, I will test you with pleasure to find out what is good.’ But that also proved to be meaningless.
‘Laughter,’ I said, ‘is madness. And what does pleasure accomplish?’
I tried cheering myself with wine, and embracing folly – my mind still guiding me with wisdom. I wanted to see what was good for people to do under the heavens during the few days of their lives.
I undertook great projects: I built houses for myself and planted vineyards.
I made gardens and parks and planted all kinds of fruit trees in them.
I made reservoirs to water groves of flourishing trees.
I bought male and female slaves and had other slaves who were born in my house. I also owned more herds and flocks than anyone in Jerusalem before me.
I amassed silver and gold for myself, and the treasure of kings and provinces. I acquired male and female singers, and a harem as well – the delights of a man’s heart.
I became greater by far than anyone in Jerusalem before me. In all this my wisdom stayed with me.
I denied myself nothing my eyes desired;
Yet when I surveyed all that my hands had done
Then I turned my thoughts to consider wisdom,
I saw that wisdom is better than folly,
The wise have eyes in their heads,
Then I said to myself,
For the wise, like the fool, will not be long remembered;
So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me. All of it is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.
I hated all the things I had toiled for under the sun, because I must leave them to the one who comes after me.

And who knows whether that person will be wise or foolish? Yet they will have control over all the fruit of my toil into which I have poured my effort and skill under the sun. This too is meaningless.
So my heart began to despair over all my toilsome labour under the sun.
For a person may labour with wisdom, knowledge and skill, and then they must leave all they own to another who has not toiled for it. This too is meaningless and a great misfortune.
What do people get for all the toil and anxious striving with which they labour under the sun?
All their days their work is grief and pain; even at night their minds do not rest. This too is meaningless.
A person can do nothing better than to eat and drink and find satisfaction in their own toil. This too, I see, is from the hand of God,
for without him, who can eat or find enjoyment?

To the person who pleases him, God gives wisdom, knowledge and happiness, but to the sinner he gives the task of gathering and storing up wealth to hand it over to the one who pleases God. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.
There is a time for everything,
a time to be born and a time to die,
a time to kill and a time to heal,
a time to weep and a time to laugh,
a time to scatter stones and a time to gather them,
a time to search and a time to give up,
a time to tear and a time to mend,
a time to love and a time to hate,
What do workers gain from their toil?
I have seen the burden God has laid on the human race.
He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the human heart; yet no-one can fathom what God has done from beginning to end.
I know that there is nothing better for people than to be happy and to do good while they live.
That each of them may eat and drink, and find satisfaction in all their toil – this is the gift of God.
I know that everything God does will endure for ever; nothing can be added to it and nothing taken from it. God does it so that people will fear him.
Whatever is has already been,
And I saw something else under the sun:
I said to myself,
